$why: The exec baseline W5's '2 processes per Bash tool call' target is defined against.

It did not exist until 2026-09-09: W5 P0 lists a fork counter as a deliverable and W5 P6 records '456 execs per Bash call to 35', and on 2026-09-09 `grep -rlnP 'strace|GUARD_PASS|HOOKS_ONLY|FORK_COUNT' .ci .claude scripts` returned ZERO files while `git ls-files | grep -iE 'strace|exec-baseline'` returned zero as well. Both numbers were unreproducible.

Every number below is DERIVED from .claude/settings.json by .claude/rediacc_hooks/execcount.py and pinned here. It counts the processes the HARNESS starts (one per hooks[].command), which is a floor on the true exec count and never the whole of it: in-guard forks are a separate measurement this file does not make.

Enforced by check:ci-hook-exec-baseline, which fails in BOTH directions. A count that GREW is a refusal. A count that SHRANK is also a refusal, saying so and printing the new value to paste, because a baseline that silently absorbs an improvement stops being able to prove the next one.

target.why: W5's stated target, recorded so the gap is a number. Today's value is in measured.tools.Bash; the gate enforces that it cannot drift without an edit here, not the target. D4 moved it from 12 to 3 on 2026-09-21: one harness command per (event, matcher) pattern, members listed in .claude/rediacc_hooks/lifecycle.py.

$why: The TRUE per-call Python process count for one Bash tool call, lifecycle fan-out included, which `measured` (harness commands only) cannot see: the harness starts 3 commands for a Bash call, and before agent/plans/PLAN-tooling-speed.md SP4 the post-bash and post-tool runners started one more Python process per member, 16 in all.
Since SP4 the advisory members of post-bash and post-tool run inside their runner (lifecycle.run_inprocess); pre-bash keeps the dispatcher, a blocking guard chain, as its one member process.

Measured by .claude/rediacc_hooks/tests/test_lifecycle_inprocess.py with a sitecustomize that logs every Python interpreter the three harness commands start; that test fails in BOTH directions when the live count leaves these numbers. REDIACC_HOOK_INPROCESS=off measures the old fan-out (16) as its control.

The two-way budgets of agent/plans/PLAN-tooling-code-reduction.md D6 (CR8): processes per Bash call, guard chain latency p50, lines per guard and test seconds per guard. Each table is {slack, max}; a measurement above `max` GREW, one under `max * (1 - slack)` SHRANK and must be repinned, so the ceilings only move down unless a change raises one by hand with its reason.

Measured from committed files only, so CI and a laptop agree: processesPerCall from perCall above, chainLatencyP50Ms from .ci/config/hook-ledger.json (the ledger snapshot), guardLines from .claude/rediacc_hooks/guards/<stem>.py, guardTestSeconds from the units of .ci/config/lane-durations.json (a unit named test_<stem>* or test-<stem>*, plus the two suites every guard shares, keyed by unit id).
Checked by `python3 .claude/hooks/stop/wl_hookreport.py --check-budgets`; `--write-budgets` lowers and adds ceilings and refuses to raise one.
stopP50Ms is OWED: the Stop p50 needs the per-check timing of PLAN-tooling-speed.md SP3, which is not on this tree. It carries no number until then, and nothing reads its absence as zero.

stopP50Ms.owed: PLAN-tooling-speed.md SP3: run_stop as a registry writing each check's duration into the blocklog row

probeTools.AskUserQuestion: the third PreToolUse matcher. Its chain is the shortest, which makes it the row that notices a guard being added to every chain by habit.
probeTools.Bash: the tool W5's '2 processes per Bash tool call' target is stated about. This row IS the target, and it is 3 today, down from 12 at the D4 collapse.
probeTools.BashOutput: not a matcher, a PROBE for the unanchored `Bash` matcher. It is the one tool in this table whose two readings disagree; see ambiguousMatchers.
probeTools.Glob: a read-only tool no PreToolUse matcher names. Its row is the cost of the three wildcard PostToolUse entries and nothing else, so it is the floor every tool pays.
probeTools.NotebookEdit: inside the anchored Edit-family alternation. The rarest of the four, which is why it is listed rather than assumed to track Edit.
probeTools.Read: the highest-frequency tool in a session, and the floor row that a new wildcard PostToolUse entry would move first.
probeTools.Task: a subagent launch. Listed because a hook added here multiplies by the number of subagents, not by the number of turns. It grew from 1 to 2 on 2026-09-24, deliberately: the `pre-agent` pattern (matcher `^(Agent|Task)$`) runs the spawn-time guards, first the writer cap (retired by agent/plans/PLAN-unlimited-writers.md) and now block_plan_concurrency and warn_writer_brief.
probeTools.TodoWrite: a wildcard-only tool whose name contains `Write`; it is the anchored-alternation counterpart of BashOutput and it is NOT ambiguous, which is the evidence that anchoring is what removes the ambiguity.

BashOutput.why: BLOCKER: the `Bash` matcher in .claude/settings.json is bare, and nothing here documents whether the harness matches with search or fullmatch. Under search, `Bash` also selects `BashOutput`; under fullmatch it does not. The two readings differ by 2 processes, down from 9 before the D4 collapse. Anchoring the matcher to `^Bash$` would resolve it, as its own box.
